QF.id: SIA Social Impact Assessment and Assessors_30

question.text: An SIA is offered a second engagement by the same SE — Grameen Urja Pvt Ltd — a rural solar FPE — for SAS 500 assessment, while the SIA has already conducted a prior SAS 500 engagement for the same SE two years ago. Which ethical principle is most directly engaged?

answer.text: Independence and objectivity, including consideration of familiarity threat and conflict of interest

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 5.2(e) and Section 5.9 jointly require Independence — 'Impact Assessors should be independent of the activity being audited... and should in all cases act in a manner that is free from bias and conflict of interest.' Repeat engagements raise familiarity threats; objectivity is the companion principle. Other CoC values are relevant but secondary. The Trap: Cultural sensitivity (A), constructive feedback (C), and non-judgmental attitude (D) are all CoC values but don't specifically address the repeat-engagement familiarity threat. Cross-Exam Context: NISM X-A / X-B (IA) has similar independence rules around long-tenure client relationships; XXIII applies them via SAS framework and CoC. Assessor's Pro-Tip: When taking on a repeat engagement, document specific safeguards (rotation of engagement leader, fresh team member inclusion, peer-review oversight) — ICAI SIAB's inspection framework flags un-rotated repeat engagements as a material independence risk.
